title: Plan the talk
pitch: About 3 minutes. A hard talk tends to end the way it starts, so this helps you plan a soft opening, the one thing you want heard, and how to pause before it turns into a fight.

cards.prompt: About 3 minutes. A hard talk tends to end the way it starts, so this helps you plan a soft opening, the one thing you want heard, and how to pause before it turns into a fight.
How do you feel right now?
cards.why: A number now lets you see whether planning took some of the dread out.

cards.short: what I want them to hear
cards.prompt: If they remember one thing you said, what should it be?
cards.why: Knowing your one point keeps the talk from drifting into old fights.
options: I'm on your side, even when I'm upset
I want us to sort this out together
I'm not trying to blame you
I miss feeling close to you
This matters to me, and so do you

cards.prompt: Write your opening: how you feel, about what, and what you need.
cards.why: Starting with how you feel, not what they did, makes it easier for them to listen.

cards.prompt: Write the line you'll say to take a break, with a time to come back.
cards.why: Having the words ready makes a break feel like care instead of walking out.
options: I need 20 minutes, then let's keep going.
I'm getting too worked up. Can we pick this up after dinner?
Let me take a walk and come back in half an hour.
I want to get this right. Can we pause until tonight?

cards.prompt: How do you feel right now?
cards.why: Comparing with the start shows you what having a plan did.
